title: Speech by Governor Brainard on why climate change matters for monetary policy and financial stability - Federal Reserve Board
关键词: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
Central Banks and Supervisors Network for Greening the Financial System
主要内容: Federal Reserve Governor Lael Brainard emphasized the role of climate change in shaping monetary policy and financial stability during a speech at the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco on November 8, 2019. She highlighted the risks posed by climate-related events, such as the Kincade fire, to the financial system and broader economy. Climate change is expected to increase extreme weather events, raise temperatures, and cause sea level rise, impacting homeownership costs and mortgage risk profiles. Brainard noted that climate risks may affect the Fed's responsibilities in monetary policy, financial stability, and regulation. She also referenced the 1970s and 1980s oil price shocks to illustrate the difficulty policymakers face in evaluating inflation and output effects. Climate change and its policy responses could influence long-term productivity and economic growth, affecting the neutral real interest rate. Private-sector businesses, including insurance companies, are working to understand and disclose climate risks to investors and financial institutions. The Carbon Disclosure Project estimates that the 500 largest companies by market capitalization are exposed to nearly $1 trillion in risk, with half expected to materialize within five years.
